claims.statement: The attacker told BleepingComputer the breach began with an exposed GitLab configuration file on an Internet Archive development server, reported as exposed since at least December 2022.
That token gave access to the source code, which held more credentials and tokens used to reach the user database and the Zendesk support system.
A second breach in October 2024 used a Zendesk token that had not been rotated after earlier warnings.

unresolvedQuestions: Primary source needed: an Internet Archive statement on the root cause.
The 7TB and 31 million account figures come from the attacker and breach-notification services; attribute them, do not state them as confirmed.

claims.statement: The New York Times said the data and source code posted on 4chan in June 2024 were taken from its GitHub repositories in January 2024.
The Times said a credential to a cloud-based third-party code platform was inadvertently made available; the leaker's readme claimed an exposed GitHub token.
GitGuardian reported that the Times confirmed to it that a publicly leaked GitHub token was the root cause.

unresolvedQuestions: Primary source needed: The New York Times statement itself.
Leak size figures (about 270GB, 5,000+ repositories) come from the leaked archive; attribute them.
